title: Understanding Loss Function
text: The loss function, denoted as L(θ), measures how well the model predicts the target values. It is often used to guide the optimization process. Consider how the loss changes between iterations.

title: Gradient Descent Step
text: In gradient descent, the update rule for θ is $$\operatorname{\theta}\left(t+1\right)$$ $$=$$ θ(t) - \alpha * gradient. Here, \alpha is the learning rate, which is given as $$1$$. Use this to understand how θ changes between iterations.

title: Calculating $$\operatorname{\theta}\left(t+1\right)$$

title: Loss Function at θ(2)
text: You know L(θ(2)) $$=$$ $$0.5$$. Consider how the loss function might change between θ(1) and θ(2).

title: Determining L(θ(1))
